1	\section{Beam Search Compatibility}
2	\label{app:beam-search}
3	
4	OntoCoDec's constraint enforcement is designed to be decoding-strategy agnostic.
5	The main experiments (\S\ref{sec:experiments}) use greedy decoding; Appendix~\ref{app:sampling} validates nucleus sampling.
6	Here we verify compatibility with beam search, completing coverage of the three standard decoding strategies.
7	
8	\paragraph{Implementation challenges.}
9	Two stateful components require adaptation for beam search.
10	(1)~The grammar layer (XGrammar) maintains an internal \texttt{GrammarMatcher} state that tracks the generated token sequence; beam reordering invalidates this state because beams are permuted across steps.
11	Our solution instantiates a fresh \texttt{GrammarMatcher} per beam per step and replays the beam's current token sequence through XGrammar's stateless accept API (64 lines of code).
12	(2)~The semantic layer's \texttt{TypeConstraintProcessor} accumulates entity and relation registries that assume a single generation path.
13	Our solution isolates state per beam by calling \texttt{detect()} on the full partial output at each step, reconstructing all entity/relation state from scratch for each beam independently (61 lines of code).
14	Both adaptations add ${\sim}125$ lines total without modifying the existing greedy/sampling logic.
15	
16	\paragraph{Results.}
17	Table~\ref{tab:beam-search} compares beam search ($k{=}4$, \texttt{early\_stopping=True}) against greedy decoding under full S1 constraints across six model-dataset combinations.

OntoCoDec's constraint enforcement is designed to be decoding-strategy agnostic.

\paragraph{Implementation challenges.}
Two stateful components require adaptation for beam search.
(1)~The grammar layer (XGrammar) maintains an internal \texttt{GrammarMatcher} state that tracks the generated token sequence; beam reordering invalidates this state because beams are permuted across steps.

% Section 5 — SciERC Results (Draft)
% Data source: Phase 2 SciERC registry experiments
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_unconstrained, phase2_scierc_grammar_only,
%          phase2_scierc_semantic_only, phase2_scierc_full_s1, phase2_scierc_full_s2
% All numbers verified against registry 2026-05-14.

\subsection{Ablation and Composability with Fine-Tuning}
\label{sec:scierc-results}

Table~\ref{tab:scierc-ablation} presents the five-way ablation on SciERC (Qwen3-8B, zero-shot, 551 documents); only the active constraint layers differ across rows.

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  Table: SciERC five-way ablation
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small

& \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{F1}} \\

\midrule

\end{tabular}}%
\caption{Five-way ablation on SciERC (551 docs, Qwen3-8B, zero-shot).
$\Delta$DR: relative change vs.\ unconstrained.
Tot.\ = DR + CF (total type-violation burden).
Best per column in \textbf{bold} (CF excluded; Tot.\ included).
F1 $\times$100. Bootstrap: 10{,}000 iterations.
S1 = single-pass (\S\ref{sec:strategies}), S2 = two-pass (\S\ref{sec:s2}).
Grammar-only represents the ceiling of grammar-constrained decoding~\cite{geng2023gcd}: vocabulary membership is enforced but cross-field semantic constraints are not.}
\label{tab:scierc-ablation}
\end{table}

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (a) Core result
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{Zero-shot diagnostic.}
% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: DR=0.1537; phase2_scierc_full_s1: DR=0.0093
% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: R-F1=0.0823; phase2_scierc_full_s1: R-F1=0.0836
% bootstrap: delta=+0.13pp, CI=[-0.24,+0.58], p=0.5824
Full S1 reduces DR from 15.37\% to 0.93\% ($\downarrow$94\%) while R-F1 is unchanged (8.23\,$\to$\,8.36, $p{=}0.58$).
Per-relation DR drops to $\leq$2.82\%, reaching 0\% on 4/7 relations (Appendix~\ref{app:per-relation-landscape}).
Post-hoc filtering achieves slightly higher F1 via precision gains but discards up to 48\% of predictions including true positives (Appendix~\ref{app:posthoc-extended}).
CF rises from 0.08\% to 9.90\% (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (b) Grammar layer
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{Layer contributions.}
% phase2_scierc_grammar_only: RV=0, ET=0, DR=0.1484, R-F1=0.0823
Grammar-only eliminates RV and ET with no F1 impact while DR remains at 14.84\%, the ceiling of grammar-based decoding~\cite{geng2023gcd}; grammar-only CF is near-zero (0.08\%), so CF originates from the semantic layer.
Semantic-only reduces DR by only 24\% and cannot eliminate RV or ET; this is the \emph{enabling dependency}: adding the grammar layer yields a further 92\% reduction (11.65\%\,$\to$\,0.93\%).

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (d) S1 vs S2
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{S1 vs.\ S2.}
S2 achieves comparable DR (0.97\%) but lower R-F1 (8.03 vs.\ 8.36) with fewer triples (1{,}644 vs.\ 1{,}729) and does not resolve the CF trade-off (8.03\% vs.\ 9.90\%); we adopt S1 as the primary configuration.
% phase2_scierc_full_s2: DR=0.0097, R-F1=0.0803, CF=0.0803, triples=1644

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (e) Composability with Fine-Tuning
%  exp_ids: w5_lora_scierc_unconstrained_eval, w5_lora_scierc_constrained_eval,
%           w5_llama_lora_scierc_unconstrained_eval, w5_llama_lora_scierc_constrained_eval,
%           w5_qwen_docred_lora_unconstrained_eval, w5_qwen_docred_lora_constrained_eval,
%           w5_llama_docred_lora_unconstrained_eval, w5_llama_docred_lora_constrained_eval
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{Composability with fine-tuning.}
\label{sec:composability}
Fine-tuning alone reduces DR to 1--2\% but leaves residual violations that vary by schema tightness (Table~\ref{tab:composability}).
On SciERC ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.333$), adding S1 eliminates or near-eliminates DR: Qwen 1.95\%\,$\to$\,0\%, Llama 1.11\%\,$\to$\,0.09\%, with R-F1 within $\pm$0.1\,pp.
On DocRED ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$, 96 relations), S1 reduces DR from 0.76\% to 0.01\% (Qwen, $\downarrow$99\%) and 0.49\% to 0.21\% (Llama, $\downarrow$57\%); R-F1 changes are $-$0.30\,pp and $+$0.06\,pp.
The lower Llama-DocRED reduction (57\% vs.\ 92--100\%) traces to higher tightness ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$), which triggers grammar-first fallback more frequently.
Across all four model-dataset settings, DR\,$\leq$\,0.21\% with R-F1 within $\pm$0.6\,pp.
CF interference drops from $+$9.82\,pp (zero-shot SciERC) to $+$1.18\,pp (fine-tuned), tracing to \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$X ambiguity (Appendix~\ref{app:cf-distribution}); the semantic layer alone accounts for 39--72\% of DR reduction under fine-tuning (\S\ref{sec:composition}).
LoRA + greedy S1 is the recommended fast deployment configuration: DR\,$\leq$\,0.21\%, CF\,$\leq$\,1.2\% at R-F1 40--46, with $+$10\% latency overhead (\S\ref{sec:runtime}).
Beam search ($k{=}4$) with LoRA eliminates all four violation types on SciERC for both Qwen and Llama (R-F1 44.23, 46.11; \S\ref{sec:beam-results}).

Beam search on DocRED (zero-shot, 50 documents) introduces a modest increase in parse failures (3/50, 6\%) compared to greedy (1.1\%), as longer beam-generated sequences occasionally produce malformed JSON in complex documents.
With DR=0 in 50 DocRED documents for both calibrated models, the Clopper-Pearson 95\% CI upper bound is 5.8\%; the full-scale LoRA evaluation below (998 documents, CI${\approx}$0.3\%) provides stronger statistical confirmation.

Table~\ref{tab:beam-docred-lora} reports LoRA + beam-4 results on the full DocRED dev set (998 documents), extending the fine-tuning composability evaluation from SciERC to the higher-$\bar{\kappa}$ regime.
Parse failure rates under LoRA beam-4 range from 1.3\% to 3.5\%, lower than the zero-shot rate.

Llama-3.1-8B achieves zero violations across all four metrics (ET, RV, DR, CF = 0\%) on DocRED with LoRA + beam-4, extending the zero-violation result from SciERC to the high-$\bar{\kappa}$ regime.
Qwen3-8B achieves DR=0\% with near-zero CF (0.01\%); R-F1 is preserved ($\pm$0.06\,pp).
Combined with the sampling robustness results (Appendix~\ref{app:sampling}), these findings confirm that OntoCoDec's constraint enforcement is compatible with greedy, sampling, and beam search decoding without modification to the core constraint logic.
